newsitem.title: USA: Atlas mill plan gets favorable recommendation.
newsitem.headline: Atlas mill plan gets favorable recommendation.

text.p: Atlas Corp said on Tuesday it received a favorable recommendation from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission regarding a proposed reclamation plan for its uranium mill site in Utah.

The commission's final Technical Evaluation Report concluded Atlas's proposed plan met regulatory requirements and would ultimately allow the company to reliquish its responsibility for the site, the company said.
The uranium mill, which operated from 1956 until 1984, was bought by Atlas in 1962. Atlas finished demolishing and disposing of the mill facilities in 1966.
Under the plan, the mill tailings pile, or the radioactive waste, would be recontoured and covered with earth and rock to control radon emanations and prevent erosions, Atlas said.
Atlas estimated it would cost another $13 million to $15 million to fulfill the plan. Atlas's share of this sum would be 44 percent, the company said.
Alternative plans for off-site reclamation were estimated to cost about $200 million, the company said.
Atlas said, under the 1992 Comprehensive National Energy Policy Act, the federal government would reimburse 56 percent of past and future reclamation-related expenses.
The company filed its original reclamation plan in 1988.
